_comment: G-8: every display string in the game, English only in MVP. Keys are ui_<screen>_<element> or n_<event>_title/_body (doc 08's event ids). Full table is authored alongside the screens; the entries below fix the conventions and the load-bearing templates.
_plural_rule: A template may carry a <key>_one variant, used when its count argument is exactly 1 (English needs two forms; 0 and 2+ take the base key, so the base is written in the plural). The count is the template s only numeric placeholder; a template with several names its selector in a sibling <key>_plural entry. UIConfig.t() applies this; tests/test_ui_strings.gd holds the file to it.
_source: docs/design/12-ui-ux.md §3.1 + §8. Placeholders are {named} only — never positional %s. Lookup is Str.t(key, args). A missing key returns the key itself in a debug build and is a test failure (doc 12 test 21).

ui_level_1_intent: A city is people and the wire that keeps their lights on. Put up some houses, then feed them.
ui_level_1_teaches: Teaches: the build sheet, and the transformer a new lot needs before anyone can live on it.
ui_level_2_intent: Houses pay tax. Shops pay more, and give the people in the houses somewhere to work.
ui_level_2_teaches: Teaches: the commercial cards, and upgrading what already stands instead of building more of it.
ui_level_3_intent: Every building you own costs money every hour, and the street outside it costs money once. Decide what the city charges.
ui_level_3_teaches: Teaches: apartments, laying your own streets, the tax slider, and the happiness it buys or spends.
ui_level_4_intent: Something will fail. Have somebody standing by before it does.
ui_level_4_teaches: Teaches: stations and coverage, the incident drawer, keeping what you own in repair, and holding a city together for a full day.
ui_level_5_intent: You have run out of ground and you are drinking somebody else's water. Buy the first and build the second.
ui_level_5_teaches: Teaches: buying land, the development pipeline, and your first water works.
ui_level_6_intent: The ground is full and the ladder is not. Put a tower on land you already own, and take one building all the way to the top of it.
ui_level_6_teaches: Teaches: high-rises, the level-6 tower tier, and the power and water a tall building drinks.
ui_level_7_intent: You built it. Now bring all of it up: one building of every type in the city, taken up a level. The council pays for the graduation.
ui_level_7_teaches: Teaches: the city as one asset — the stations and the works you have been paying for since day one, not just the ones that pay you back.

_comment_site_scan: Wave 28 fix (doc 12 D-127). `where CAN this go` — the sentence the placement bar prints under a BLOCKED ghost, from BuildController.placement_sites(). The player, 2026-09-05, asked to create a water source and had no legal tile within forty tiles of his plant; every refusal he could see was about the ONE tile under his finger. These five say what the window says.

_comment_water_panel: S19, the water panel (doc 12 D-124, Wave 28). The chain, the mains that are open, the buildings that are too dry to upgrade, and the three verbs.
ui_water_zone_reading: Zone {zone} · {band} · supplies {supply} against {demand} · {spare} spare · buffer {buffer} h
ui_water_no_zone: This node is not joined to any main — it supplies nothing.
ui_water_advice_binds: {stage} is the narrowest part of this chain, at {m3h}. Raise {at} and the zone gets more water — anything else buys none.
ui_water_advice_binds_next: {stage} is the narrowest part of this chain, at {m3h}. Raise {at} and the zone gets more water — up to {next_m3h}, where {next} takes over.
ui_water_advice_mains: The mains at the plant bind this zone at {m3h}. A bigger pump moves nothing until a trunk main can carry it — lay one from the Utility tab.
ui_water_advice_place: This zone has no {stage} at all. Build one before anything downstream can move.
ui_water_advice_leak: {count} broken mains here are losing {leak} into the ground. Stopping the biggest costs {cost} — do that before buying capacity.
ui_water_advice_none: Every stage of this chain has room. Nothing here needs buying.
ui_water_advice_no_zone: No pressure zone — run a main to this site.
ui_water_advice_dead: This zone has no live pump or tank, so it supplies nothing at all.

_comment_water_building_row: D-125's one-row WATER summary on S5, the twin of ui_power_row above it. Same three shapes the POWER row has: served, served-but-far, and not served at all. The FAR row is the one that earns its place — doc 92 §67.8 measured a zone at pressure 1.00 refusing a high-rise whose own tile sat at 0.50, and nothing on any screen said the word `tiles` until this row did.
ui_water_row_far: Water · zone {zone} · {pct} here — {tiles} tiles from a main
ui_water_unserved: No water main reaches this building. Lay one from the Utility tab, or it stays dry.
_comment_water_siting: Doc 05 §6's placement refusals, saying WHY (doc 12 D-126). E_NO_SITE used to be the whole sentence.
_comment_water_headroom_arms: Doc 05 §2.11 refuses an upgrade on TWO arms behind one code, and they want opposite purchases (Wave 28, A91-D-147). The old single remedy — add a pump or a tank — was wrong for both at once.
ui_requirement_e_water_headroom_capacity: {stage} is the narrowest part of this zone's supply. Raise it — a pump or a tank buys nothing while something upstream is the limit.
ui_requirement_e_water_headroom_mains: The mains at the plant carry less than the plant makes. Lay a trunk main from the Utility tab; a bigger pump behind a thin pipe delivers the pipe.
ui_requirement_e_water_headroom_pressure: The zone has water to spare — this building is {tiles} tiles from the nearest main and only sees {pressure}. Lay a main closer to it.
ui_requirement_e_water_headroom_no_zone: No water main reaches this building at all. Lay one from the Utility tab before it can grow.
